course_name_original: Graphical mapping of electrical devices and grids using CAD programs
course_name_en: Graphical mapping of electrical devices and grids using CAD programs

learning_outcomes.text: Basic methods of analysis used in electrical engineering, both technical and economic aspects.
Basic principles of mapping mechanical structures and electrical diagrams. Knows the principles of designing mechanical and mechatronic systems.
General principles of creating technical documentation and managing the design process using computer-aided design and modeling tools for electromechanical systems.
Principles used in technical drawing, both in the field of mechanics and electrical engineering.
Acquire and properly select information from literature, databases, and other appropriately chosen sources, also published in foreign languages, for calculations and analyses.
Read and create graphical technical documentation in digital and paper versions.
Design a basic mechanical and electromechanical system, with particular emphasis on cooperation between the mechanical and electrical parts. For this purpose, dedicated software is used.
Recognize non-technical aspects of the design process in company activities, including economic, legal, and OHS aspects.

Independently solve technical problems in the scope of preparing technical documentation. Is aware of economic aspects in electrical engineering. Is committed to continuous development and learning due to the constant development of their field.

Direct communication with other participants in the process related to technical documentation preparation. Teamwork in carrying out tasks related to technical documentation preparation and building task teams, dividing and performing tasks in group work.

syllabus_topics: Standards and legal acts used in creating technical documentation.
Principles of correct representation of structures.
Elements of electrical technical drawing – symbols used in drawings.
AutoCAD – a tool for creating drawing documentation in 2D and 3D space.
Automation of the drawing process – creating blocks with attributes.
Using drawings in dwg format as a background for creating installation plans.
Introduction to 3D by using local coordinate systems.
CAD software dedicated for electricians for engineering analysis.
Types of electrical documentation: designs of installations, networks, electrical devices, AKPiA (Automation, Control, Measurement, and Protection).
Using AutoCAD, EPLAN and SEE Electrical Expert programs in the practice of an electrical engineer.
Creating diagrams of high-current parts of installations and AKPiA parts.
Creating cable harnesses and checking routing correctness using 3D modules.
assessment_rules: To obtain a positive final grade, it is necessary to successfully complete the laboratory classes. Students participate in laboratory classes by performing individual exercises and tasks, which are subject to evaluation. The result of the task execution serves as a report from the exercise, which is also evaluated. Each student is obliged to pass two tests during the semester and successfully complete the final project. To receive a positive grade, all tests and the project must be passed with a positive grade. The grade from the laboratory exercises is the final grade.
